verdicts_or_reports.expected: Modulo should return the remainder: 100 % 13 = 9, 47 % 20 = 7, 19.5 % 4 = 3.5, and with a = 50, a % 14 = 8 (per Help section "Modulo: 10 % 3 evaluates to 1").
verdicts_or_reports.observed: All modulo lines evaluate to "Err" (error popup says "Unexpected number"). The parser consumes "100 %" as a percent token and then chokes on "13", so the % operator no longer works as modulo; only the percentage line 250 + 20% = 300 still works.
steps: Open the Remainders file from the home screen
Look at line 2: '47 % 20' -> Err, line 3: '19.5 % 4' -> Err, line 5: 'a % 14' -> Err
Tap the Err on line 1: the error tooltip reads 'Unexpected number'

verdicts_or_reports.element: Date gaps row subtitle in PINNED section
verdicts_or_reports.expected: Pinning (or locking) a file is not a content edit, so the MODIFIED timestamp should stay JAN 05, 2026. When unpinned, the file should return to its place among the other JAN 05, 2026 files (newest-first order should not change).
verdicts_or_reports.observed: After tapping Pin on Date gaps, its MODIFIED timestamp changed from "JAN 05, 2026" to the current time "12:15 PM". After unpinning such a file it then sorts to the top of ALL FILES (e.g. Number bases, created JAN 06, jumped above newer files after being pinned/unpinned), so the home list order is no longer newest-first. Locking shows the same effect (Temperatures was changed to 12:07 PM just by locking).
steps: On the home screen, note Date gaps subtitle: 'MODIFIED: JAN 05, 2026 • CREATED: JAN 05, 2026'
Tap the Date gaps row's More options > Pin
Scroll to the top: Date gaps now shows 'MODIFIED: 12:15 PM • CREATED: JAN 05, 2026' even though its content was never edited
Unpin it: it now sorts to the top of ALL FILES instead of its JAN 05 position

verdicts_or_reports.element: Time differences row subtitle (top of ALL FILES)
verdicts_or_reports.expected: Locking only changes the lock flag. The file's content is untouched, so MODIFIED should stay JAN 04, 2026 and the file should keep its position in the date-modified list (it was between Percentages and Remainders, near the bottom).
verdicts_or_reports.observed: Before locking, Time differences showed "MODIFIED: JAN 04, 2026 • CREATED: JAN 04, 2026" and sat near the bottom of the list. After tapping More options > Lock, its subtitle became "MODIFIED: 12:21 PM • CREATED: JAN 04, 2026" and it jumped to the very top of the list, as if its content had just been edited. (File info also shows a current "Last modified at" time.) Pinning has the same effect.
steps: On the home screen, note Time differences: 'MODIFIED: JAN 04, 2026 • CREATED: JAN 04, 2026' (near the bottom of newest-first list)
Tap its More options (three-dot) button and choose Lock
Observe the row now shows 'Locked' and 'MODIFIED: 12:21 PM • CREATED: JAN 04, 2026'
Observe the row has jumped to the top of ALL FILES, although its lines are unchanged
Unlock it again: the MODIFIED value stays at the new time instead of reverting

sign_off.notes: Swept all nine files against the stated starting data. Verified: Expenses total 1,625.75 / avg 541.92; Monthly budget 2,800.50, 49.50, grand_total 2,850 (salary/gift edits propagate correctly); Temperatures and Temperature sums conversions; Number bases; Date gaps; Time differences; Percentages (36, 204, 8.50, 102, 8) including variable edits updating dependent lines immediately. Variables resolve strictly top-to-bottom (forward/undefined references error, re-assignment handled correctly) in both files and scratchpad. Pin keeps files in a PINNED section at the top under every sort order (modified/created/name, asc/desc) and survives rotation/background/rename; unpin removes the section when empty; lock shows "Locked", disables rename/delete/clear, blocks edits, survives background/rotation, and is enforced when reopened via search. One confirmed bug filed and logged: modulo (%) is broken in Remainders (100 % 13, 47 % 20, 19.5 % 4, a % 14 all show Err / "Unexpected number" instead of 9, 7, 3.5, 8) because a % after an operand is now consumed as a percentage token; 250 + 20% = 300 still correct. One observation reported twice but not accepted by dev: pinning/locking refreshes the file's MODIFIED timestamp, which also moves the file to the top of the date-modified list after unpinning.
